seo.metaDescription: ChartsProvider sets the locale and currency; useChart, useFormat and useRegisterPoints let you draw your own marks.

props.markdown: `BarChart` and `LineChart` read their number formats from a provider, and a mark of your own can do the same. This page covers `ChartsProvider`, which sets the locale and currency for everything inside it, and the three hooks you need to draw something the library does not: `useChart`, `useFormat` and `useRegisterPoints`.

Put `ChartsProvider` once near the top of the page. `locale` is a BCP 47 tag and `currency` an ISO 4217 code. Every chart, `Stat`, `Meter` and axis below it formats numbers, dates and currency that way, so the same data reads naturally for each audience. Without a provider the defaults are `en-US` and `USD`.

The `Stat` and both charts share one provider: thousands are separated with a dot, the decimal separator is a comma and the euro sign follows the number. Nothing is passed to the charts except `format="currency"`. The props are plain values, so this example also renders in a Server Component; see [Getting started](/docs/getting-started) for the charts used here and [LineChart](/docs/line-chart) for series.

`locale` changes numbers and dates; `messages` changes the words the charts speak on their own: "No data", the keyboard hint, the "1 of 6" position, target text, the column headers of the hidden data table and the default Runway status. Pass an object of plain strings, with `{placeholders}` where a value goes. Any key you leave out keeps its English default, and a key set to `undefined` does too. The strings are not functions, so a Server Component can pass them to the provider.

The order of precedence is the prop of one chart (`empty`, `keyboardHint`, `targetLabel`, `totalLabel`, `dataTable.columns`), then the provider's `messages`, then English. A column header taken from a string accessor (`y="grossMargin"` reads "Gross margin") stays the field name; `messages` supplies the header only when the accessor is a function or the chart names the column itself. A nested provider without `messages` inherits its parent's, so `<ChartsProvider currency="EUR">` inside a translated provider keeps the translation. One with `messages` replaces them instead of merging: any key it leaves out goes back to English, not to the parent's text. `locale` and `currency` don't inherit: each provider sets its own, with `en-US` and `USD` as the defaults.

The provider remembers your object by identity. An inline object, `messages={{ noData: '…' }}` in a Client Component, is a new object on every render of the parent, so every chart under it renders again. Define the object outside the component or wrap it in `useMemo`. In a Server Component this does not matter.

The unit suffixes of the `pts` and `hours` format presets are not messages; use a custom `format` function for those units in another language (see [Formatting](/docs/formatting)). The wording of the English defaults below is not public API and can change in a minor release; the keys are.

| Key | English default | Where it is used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noData` | `No data` | An empty chart, bar or meter. Also the cell text for a missing heatmap value. |
| `noValue` | `no value` | A table cell with nothing in it, read by screen readers next to the dash. |
| `keyboardHint` | `Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.` | Read when a chart takes keyboard focus. An empty string removes the hint. |
| `keyboardHintSelect` | `Press Enter to select.` | Appended to `keyboardHint`, after one space, when the point can be selected. |
| `position` | `{index} of {total}` | The live-region position of a point. Placeholders: `{index}`, `{total}`. |
| `target` | `target {value}` | A target in a spoken value, such as "40, target 50". Placeholder: `{value}`. |
| `targetLabel` | `Target {value}` | The default text under a Meter's target tick. Placeholder: `{value}`. |
| `now` | `Now` | The Now line of a RunwayChart. |
| `total` | `Total` | The total column and row of a Heatmap, and the end row of a WaterfallChart. |
| `headerItem` | `Item` | A column header of a chart's hidden data table. A header taken from a string accessor keeps the field name. |
| `headerValue` | `Value` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerCategory` | `Category` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerDate` | `Date` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerPeriod` | `Period` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerGroup` | `Group` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerRankedDetails` | `Details` | The data-table column of a RankedBars `meta`. |
| `headerColumn` | `Column` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerChange` | `Change` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerTotal` | `Total` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerPlan` | `Plan` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerActual` | `Actual` | A data-table column header. |
| `headerDifference` | `Difference` | The ComparisonBars data-table column of plan minus actual. |
| `headerRange` | `Range` | The data-table column of a LineChart band. |
| `headerRow` | `Row` | The row name of a Heatmap that has no label. |
| `headerName` | `Name` | A RunwayChart data-table column header. |
| `headerRunwayDetail` | `Detail` | The data-table column of a RunwayChart row's `sublabel`. |
| `headerRunsOut` | `Runs out` | A RunwayChart data-table column header. |
| `headerResets` | `Resets` | A RunwayChart data-table column header. |
| `headerProjectedAtReset` | `Projected at reset` | A RunwayChart data-table column header. |
| `headerStatus` | `Status` | A RunwayChart data-table column header. |
| `statusDisconnected` | `Disconnected` | Default status of a RunwayChart row whose source is disconnected. |
| `statusNoForecast` | `No forecast` | Default status of a RunwayChart row without a forecast. |
| `statusRunsOut` | `Runs out {date}` | Default status line of a RunwayChart row. Placeholder: `{date}`. |
| `statusAtReset` | `~{percent}% at reset` | Default status line when a RunwayChart row does not run out. Placeholder: `{percent}`. |
| `statusResets` | `Resets {date}` | Default status line of a RunwayChart row's reset. Placeholder: `{date}`. |
| `legendProjectedUse` | `Projected use` | RunwayChart legend. |
| `legendUnderShare` | `under {shares}%` | RunwayChart legend, after the shades. Placeholder: `{shares}`, the level edges as percentages, such as "25, 50, 75, 100". |
| `legendRunsOut` | `Runs out` | RunwayChart legend. |
| `legendLocked` | `Locked until reset` | RunwayChart legend. |
| `legendReset` | `Reset` | RunwayChart legend. |
| `legendNoForecast` | `New window, no forecast` | RunwayChart legend. |
| `onPlan` | `On plan` | The change a ComparisonBars row shows when actual is within the tolerance. |
| `planActual` | `{label}, plan {plan}, actual {actual}, {delta}` | A ComparisonBars row read aloud. Placeholders: `{label}`, `{plan}`, `{actual}`, `{delta}`. |
| `waterfallStep` | `{label}, {text}, running total {total}` | A WaterfallChart step read aloud. Placeholders: `{label}`, `{text}`, `{total}`. |
| `chartRole` | `chart` | What a screen reader calls an interactive chart (`aria-roledescription`). |
| `runningTotalLabel` | `total` | The label of the running total in a WaterfallChart tooltip. |
| `peak` | `Peak` | The first line of a WaffleColumns callout. |
| `binAll` | `All values` | The default Heatmap legend label when there are no breaks. |
| `binUnder` | `Under {value}` | The lowest Heatmap legend bin. Placeholder: `{value}`. |
| `binRange` | `{from} to {to}` | A middle Heatmap legend bin. Placeholders: `{from}`, `{to}`. |
| `binOver` | `{value} and up` | The highest Heatmap legend bin. Placeholder: `{value}`. |
| `valueAgainst` | `{value} against {reference}` | A RangeMeter's value against its reference, read aloud. Placeholders: `{value}`, `{reference}`. |
| `valueAbove` | `above {max}` | A ZoneMeter value above its maximum. Placeholder: `{max}`. |
| `valueBelow` | `below {min}` | A ZoneMeter value below its minimum. Placeholder: `{min}`. |
| `resetMark` | `reset` | The label next to the reset tick of a RunwayChart row. |
| `heatmapName` | `Heatmap` | The accessible name of a scrolling Heatmap that has no title. |
| `deltaUp` | `Up` | Read before a Delta's value when it went up. |
| `deltaDown` | `Down` | Read before a Delta's value when it went down. |
| `deltaFlat` | `No change` | Read before a Delta's value when it did not change. |

When none of the building blocks in [Composition](/docs/composition) draws what you need, write a component and put it inside `Chart`. `useChart()` returns the size, the margins, the data, the number formatter, the active point and the `x` and `y` scales (narrow them on `kind`: `'linear'`, `'band'`, `'point'` or `'time'`), `y2` when the chart has a second axis it can use (undefined otherwise), `useFormat()` returns formatters in the provider's locale, and `useRegisterPoints()` tells the chart where your points are.

Lollipops are not a built-in mark. `Lollipops` reads the scales with `useChart()`, labels each point with a formatter from `useFormat()`, and registers the points. That registration is what makes `NearestPointer` find them under the pointer, `Tooltip` show them and the arrow keys walk them. Focus the chart and press `Home` to hear the first one.

**Memoize the points you register.** `useRegisterPoints(points)` registers again every time the array changes identity, so build it in `useMemo` with the scales and formatter as dependencies. Each point needs a unique `id`, an `index`, the `datum`, a position in plot pixels (`x`, `y`), a `label` for screen readers and the tooltip `segments`. Hooks cannot run in a Server Component, so a file that uses any of them starts with `'use client'`.

props.text: Several React roots on one page

props.markdown: Pattern ids, for hatching and gradients, come from React's `useId`, which is only unique within one root. When charts render in separate roots (islands, micro-frontends), two charts can end up with the same pattern id. Give each chart its own `chartId`. `Chart`, the high-level charts and `Heatmap` take it.

props.code: <BarChart chartId="margin-chart" data={weeks} x="week" y="margin" title="Margin by week" />
